{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZGRNSg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhCsrt0", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 9, "title": "Fix GitHub Pages deployment failing because Pages site is not configured", "body": "## Problem

Issue [#7](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/7) was closed after [PR #8](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/pull/8) merged the GitHub Pages workflow into `main` at commit `64a53034c512d72d09003adb68d0437a5d3d1a01`. As authorized in #7's required post-merge verification, this is a **new follow-up Issue**, not a reopening of #7.

The first `main` deployment run failed **after its build/tests and artifact upload passed**, before any production deployment could occur:

- [Failed Pages workflow run](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/actions/runs/39764299327)
- [Failing deploy job](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/actions/runs/39764299327/job/119779943186)
- In that run, `checks / core` and `checks / browser` succeeded, including `actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3`.
- `deploy` failed on `actions/configure-pages@v5` (`enablement: false`); `actions/deploy-pages@v4` was skipped.
- Exact log: `Get Pages site failed. Please verify that the repository has Pages enabled and configured to build using GitHub Actions, or consider exploring the enablement parameter for this action. Error: Not Found - https://docs.github.com/rest/pages/pages#get-a-apiname-pages-site`.

Likely cause: **GitHub Pages is not yet enabled/configured for this repository.** The precise repository Pages configuration has not been independently read, so treat this as the leading diagnosis rather than a proven setting. Expected site: https://takahirox.github.io/snes-rust/. The successful pre-merge PR tests did not and could not establish live publication.

## Expected outcome

Enable the repository's Pages site with **GitHub Actions** as its deployment source, rerun the existing `main` deployment (or trigger a new authorized `main` run), and confirm the public SNES WebAssembly app is actually served successfully.

Keep the deployment workflow's scoped token permissions and the existing build/test gate; do not work around a missing repository setting by committing generated assets, moving to a `gh-pages` branch, widening privileges unnecessarily, or bundling ROMs.

## Context and reproduction

1. Open the [failed workflow run](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/actions/runs/39764299327) for `main` commit `64a5303`.
2. Observe `checks / core` and `checks / browser` succeed.
3. Observe `deploy` fail at `actions/configure-pages@v5` with a GitHub Pages REST 404; the actual deployment step is skipped.
4. The expected public site cannot be considered deployed on this run.

## Remediation tasks

- [ ] In **Settings → Pages → Build and deployment**, verify that GitHub Pages is enabled and **Source = GitHub Actions**. If the repository is not yet enabled, a maintainer with repository administration permission should configure it (or evaluate `actions/configure-pages` enablement only if appropriate and safely authorized). Document the actual setting, and check `github-pages` environment restrictions if applicable.
- [ ] Rerun the failed workflow or trigger another deployment for the current `main` commit without unrelated source changes. Check whether `configure-pages` and `deploy-pages` now succeed.
- [ ] Check the resulting HTTPS Pages URL (normally https://takahirox.github.io/snes-rust/) for the app, CSS/JS and `snes_wasm.wasm`. Verify correct content types, no 404/CSP errors, successful Wasm instantiation and enabled local ROM picker.
- [ ] Verify the published artifact contains only the intended four static app assets and does not expose commercial/homebrew ROM binaries, SRAM saves, build caches or test output.
- [ ] Record the successful Pages run URL, live URL and verification evidence in the Issue. If deployment still fails, record the **new** error and fix the actual cause with a focused PR when a code change is required.

## Acceptance and verification

- Repository Pages source is demonstrably set to GitHub Actions, and the merged workflow runs to completion.
- Deployment job reports success and a concrete Pages URL.
- A real HTTPS fetch/browser check establishes the page, its relative static assets and WebAssembly initialize under `/snes-rust/` without unexpected resource errors. Users can select a lawfully supplied local ROM; nothing is uploaded.
- Post-deployment results (success or further defects) are recorded honestly. If a code PR is required, keep all PR-pre-merge checks independently verifiable and do the **production-site smoke check after the changed workflow is deployed**; do not make a merge-triggered check a prerequisite for its own merge.

## Optional validation

Play a legally redistributable, audited diagnostic ROM locally in the live site; check a second browser or physical gamepad. Do not add copyrighted ROMs to Pages.

## Required post-merge verification

If a corrective PR is needed, verify the actual Pages deployment after that PR merges, and report the Actions URL and HTTP/browser results. This post-merge check does not block approval of the corrective PR; if it uncovers a separate issue, track that issue independently.

Related: #7, PR #8.
